I haven't noticed any major downtime in the last couple of days, and that's despite the site getting DDoSed. Maybe I'm just getting on at the right times, though.

Reddit isn't under a constant DDOS like Voat is right now. A powerful DDOS can even knock down a government website, and has. The moving to the cloud HAS fixed Voat's problem of downtime. The botnet is attacking, sure, but it's not getting through thanks to the DDOS protection; that little thing that pops up every so often saying that your browser is being checked. All the hosting in the world can't stop a DDOS attack, just resist it. Right now Voat is doing a pretty good job of that.
Cyber security is an arms race, like anything else.

1. Reddit does stumble under its load. Often.
  2. Voat cannot afford anywhere near as much DDOS resiliency.
  3. Moving to the cloud has fixed things. Or at least improved the situation. We can actually use it now, in the middle of an attack.
So is it because VOAT is not on the most premium plan offered by the hosting site?

There is a difference of scale between the two companies. Reddit is owned by a company which makes $8+ billion dollars a year.

This allows them to negotiate with their hosting provider Amazon on a much larger scale. The hosting at the scale reddit is purchasing isn't available to the average person as it's a contract negotiated between companies.

Voat on the other hand is currently run by two students. This means they have about as much access and negotiating power as you or I do.

I guess an analogy could be the difference between with you go to buy a car, and when Enterprise Car Rentals goes to buy cars. Since they are buying hundreds if not thousands of cars. Ford/GM/etc will strike a far better deal.

Voat isn't at that stage yet, they are comparatively sized to a family renta-car place in a midsized american city.

Or the hosting site can't cope with this kind of attack very well.

To compare a normal DoS attack to talking with a person:

DoSer Dial's Voat's phone number, lets it ring once and hangs up.
Voat: "This is Voat! How can I help you?"
Voat: "Hello?"
Voat: "Strange..." *hangs up*
DoSer Dial's Voat's phone number...

The hosting company helps by answering the phone for Voat, and then forwards your call if you actually stay on the line.

Unfortunately a Layer 7 attack (like what Voat is going through right now) is more like the DoSer stays on the line and has a full conversation, but they don't really care what Voat is saying just so long as they can keep Voat talking with as little input from themselves as possible.

The only reason that Voat is still usable right now is because they did this move to CloudFlare.

The move did two things for them, it allowed them to be scalable enough so that they can actually tolerate the massive influx of traffic they received throughout the Reddit mass-exodus and it allowed them to better tolerate these types of attacks.

What's currently happening is a DDOS (directed denial of service) attack. This is performed using TCP (Transmission Control Protocol) and only performing the first part of the protocol. In TCP, your computer does a three way handshake with the server. You send the first message, the server sends something back, and they wait for you to send the confirmation of their message. When a computer only does the first part of this handshake, the server creates a new process to deal with this incoming user and ends up sitting on that process taking up memory until it times out. This is dangerous because with enough traffic holding up server resources you can cause the server to run out of memory and render the service unusable or even crash the server itself.

CloudFlare specializes in this type of protection and is trying to help create a barrier between the botnet performing these attacks and the legitimate users that are trying to use the service.

What I've described up to this point is a layer 4 DDOS attack. It's important to distinguish this from a layer 7 attack. The layers of network communication follow the OSI model. Read more on it if you are interested. But the attack that Voat is seeing is actually a layer 7 attack that attacks on the application level. This means that the attack is advanced and tailored specifically for Voat. It essentially tries to flood the server with seemingly legitimate requests that it goes off and tries to fulfill. This is especially dangerous as these processes will take up far more memory than a layer 3 attack.

All in all, the move has allowed Voat to basically function and they are the victims of an attack.
So VOAT gets attacked and no one can stop, find or punish those that are causing the attack?

Essentially. Botnets are created by infecting the computers of innocent people. They create a zombie army that attack a given target. The people who own these computers are probably wondering why their internet feels a little slow all of a sudden.

Typically when they receive a lot of traffic from an address like this and it is flagged as a botnet, they just let the ISP know so that they can tell the customer to clean their computer.
